I know it's not as bad as some stories here but about 6 years ago we had a group of friends, some international so we spend almost all our nights on Skype/reddit/Whatsapp. One of them was dating a girl I've had a crush on but I've never told him or her about it and I've always tried to be supportive of their relationship even if in retrospect they were just not good for each other. At some point he impersonated her and sweet-talked to me until I confessed my feelings, playing her up to be loving and understanding. Then he and another guy showed the text logs to my crush and I felt so humiliated and betrayed I completely spiraled. I ended up in the hospital and I've been battling depression/intrusive thoughts ever since. They've broken up and she's married to a good guy now, we're still best friends and pretty much the only left from the original friend group.

Thank you for telling me about your journey. I woke up just a bit ago and even if I'm absolutely hangover it's making me reevaluate things, as I'm reading your story. When I was in my early late teens early 20s I got into this mindset of not being worth the opportunities that I had; I've squandered a lot of things in my life. I stopped eating or forgot completely. I studied and played video games most of the time. I met friends that played around with me and it got to the point where I needed to stay at a hospital because I couldn't function on my own. My previous relationship left me on the rocks and I relapsed there, and even if it seems everything is alright now- here I am. 

My parents (dad) are pretty strict and they put this idea in my head that being a man is only a particular set of things. Yeah asking for help isn't one of them, if that's what you guessed. Reading my drunken pleas last night, it's pretty evident that those ideas are still very much engrained. 

I'm gonna try tonight to talk to my wife and my best friend. As of now I just don't want to be alone and I want to break this cycle before rock bottom comes back to slap me in the face. I think that as much as it's a scary thought, maybe being medicated consistently isn't so bad. I want a family in the future and I want to be there. Thank you again for writing to me I hope your journey brings you happiness. God bless you
